chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who vowed upon himself that if he was safe from an illness, or freed from prison, that he would fast every Wednesday, and it was the day in which he was released. So he was unable to fast due to an illness that afflicted him, or other than that. So it was prolonged for the man during his lifetime, and a lot of fasts accumulated upon him. What is the expiation for that? He (peace be upon him) said: He should give in charity, for each day, with a Mudd of wheat, or the price of a Mudd.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for missed voluntary fasts accumulated from a vow due to prolonged illness?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the accumulation of missed voluntary vows is resolved through proportional charity rather than making up the fasts, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that vows of specific acts of worship can be redeemed by their equivalent value when performance becomes impossible. This highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding *nadhr* (vows), where the spiritual intent is preserved through the prescribed expiation (*kaffarah*) of feeding the poor, ensuring the vow is fulfilled without undue hardship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a man who vowed upon himself that if he was safe from an illness, or freed from prison, that he would be Fasting every day of Wednesday, and it was the day in which he was released. So he was frustrated from the Fasting due to an illness which hit him, or other than that. So it got prolonged for the man, during his lifetime, and there gathered upon him a lot of Fasts. What is the expiation for that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should give in charity, for each day, with a Mudd (approximately 750g. of food) of wheat, or the price of a Mudd (approximately 750g. of food).’
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who vows to fast, if he is released from jail, every Wednesday. It is the day when he was released but he fails to do so due to illness or other reasons; and during his lifetime a large number of days of such fast become due upon him. What is the expiation for such fast? He (the Imam) said, ‘He must pay charity of one mud (a certain measurement) of wheat or its price for every day of fast.’”
